pageCache.pageTitle: About Marymount London | UK's First All-Girls IB School
pageCache.text:
About Marymount
MARYMOUNT INTERNATIONAL SCHOOL LONDON
Founded in 1955, as the first all-girls’ school in the United Kingdom to adopt the International Baccalaureate curriculum (Middle Years Programme and IB Diploma Programme), Marymount International School London welcomes curious, motivated and academically ambitious students. Established under the auspices of the Religious of the Sacred Heart of Mary (RSHM), the school welcomes students from a diverse range of faiths and cultural backgrounds.
Located just twelve miles from central London, with excellent school and public transport links to surrounding areas, Marymount offers both day and boarding (full, weekly and flexi) options. Heathrow and Gatwick airports are both within easy reach. Long-term and short-term applications accepted.
Top 1% of IB Schools Worldwide
Consistently achieving significantly above the global points average and currently ranked in the top 1% of IB Schools worldwide, Marymount offers a broad, holistic, academically challenging programme that encourages critical thinking, collaborative learning and global contextualisation. Small classes and a stimulating teaching environment ensure that students are appropriately challenged and encouraged to develop their intellectual potential and grow in confidence as independent thinkers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Admissions | How to Apply to Marymount London in Surrey
pageCache.text:
An Exceptional Education
Take the next step towards a Marymount education
Register your daughter or join an upcoming Open Day.
An international private school that inspires confidence
Choosing the right school is one of the most important decisions a family can make. Whether you are a local family exploring schools close to home, relocating to the UK, or an international family considering boarding for your daughter, we are delighted that you are considering Marymount.
As an international private school in London, we bring together students and families from across the world, alongside those from the local area. Our students are encouraged to question, explore and think independently. They develop resilience through challenge, confidence through achievement and a lifelong love of learning that prepares them for university and beyond.
Flexible entry throughout the year
Recognising that every family’s journey is different, Marymount welcomes applications throughout the year, wherever places are available. As an international school in London, our rolling admissions process offers flexibility for families relocating from overseas, changing schools, or seeking a private boarding place outside of the traditional admissions cycle.
Where possible, we encourage families to begin the process early, particularly for popular year groups and boarding places. However, we understand that circumstances change, and we are always happy to discuss the options available.
If you are unsure when your daughter might join us, we encourage you to get in touch. A conversation is often the best place to start.
Our Admissions Process
Applying to Marymount is straightforward, and our admissions team is here to guide you at every step.

pageCache.text:
Senior School
Take the next step towards a Marymount education
Register your daughter or join an upcoming Open Day.
Building curious thinkers. Confident learners. Future changemakers.
Senior School at Marymount is a time for discovery, challenge and growth. Through the International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme (MYP), students are encouraged to think deeply, ask meaningful questions and make connections between their learning and the world around them.
In a supportive all-girls environment, each student is encouraged to discover her strengths, develop her independence and grow in confidence as a learner and as a person.
The Senior School experience
From Year 7 to Year 11 (Grades 6-10), students are known, supported and encouraged to grow — academically, personally and socially.
Learning at Marymount is active and ambitious. Our students are encouraged to ask questions, explore different perspectives and take increasing ownership of their learning, while being part of a community where they can feel a strong sense of belonging.
The International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme (MYP) provides the academic framework for Senior School, preparing students with the knowledge, skills and confidence to take their next steps.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Sixth Form at Marymount London | IB Diploma Year
pageCache.text:
Sixth Form
Take the next step towards a Marymount education
Register your daughter or join an upcoming Open Day.
A time of independence, ambition and possibility
Sixth Form at Marymount is centred on the International Baccalaureate. As an IB-only school, students in Years 12 and 13 (Grades 11 and 12) follow either the full IB Diploma Programme (IBDP) or a programme of IB Diploma Courses, allowing for an academically ambitious pathway shaped around individual strengths, interests and future plans.
These final two years of school bring greater independence, deeper academic engagement and growing confidence. Students are encouraged to take increasing ownership of their learning, explore their interests in greater depth and begin shaping the direction they wish to take beyond Marymount.
Within a close-knit international community, academic challenge is balanced with individual support, leadership opportunities and personal growth, preparing students to move confidently into university and life beyond school.
The Sixth Form experience
Growing independenceSixth Form students take increasing responsibility for their learning, choices and goals, developing the habits and confidence needed for life beyond school.
Finding directionGreater academic choice and depth allow students to explore their interests and begin making informed decisions about university, future study and careers.
Developing a voiceStudents are encouraged to contribute ideas, lead, collaborate and participate fully in the life of the School.
A global communityLearning alongside students from different cultures and backgrounds encourages open-mindedness, intercultural understanding and a genuinely international outlook. This reflects Marymount’s existing positioning of the Sixth Form experience as one shaped by diverse perspectives and global awareness.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts at Marymount London | Drama, Dance and Music
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
Creativity, confidence and connection
At Marymount, every student experiences the Performing Arts. Through music, dance and theatre, students develop confidence, creativity, collaboration and self-expression while gaining a deeper understanding of cultures, communities and the world around them. The Performing Arts are not reserved for a select few. They are an essential part of a Marymount education, helping every student discover their voice, build lifelong skills and develop as confident global citizens.
Why Performing Arts?
The Performing Arts are about far more than performance.
Through music, dance and theatre students learn to communicate, collaborate, think creatively and engage with different cultures and perspectives. They develop resilience, confidence and the ability to express ideas while building skills that support success across all areas of life.
At Marymount, every student participates in the performing arts because these experiences help students understand themselves, understand others and understand the role creativity plays in society.
The Marymount approach to Performing Arts
The defining feature of Performing Arts at Marymount is that every student participates. Every student experiences:
Music
Dance
Performance
Creative collaboration
Global perspectives through the Arts
Students explore artistic traditions and performance styles from around the world.
Students learn how artists respond to society and how the arts help us understand cultures, histories and communities.
Japanese Kabuki Theatre
British Punch and Judy
Italian Commedia dell’Arte
International dance traditions
Contemporary performance practice
The Performing Arts journey
Students learn how artists respond to society and how the arts help us understand cultures, histories and communities. Focus areas include:
Performance skills
Ensemble work
Communication
Artistic confidence
Collaboration
Performing Arts in action

pageCache.pageTitle: Art and Design at Marymount London | IB Visual Arts School
pageCache.text:
Art & Design
A word from our Head of Art & Design
“Art & Design at Marymount encourages students to think creatively, communicate meaningfully and engage deeply with the world around them. Students learn to observe, question, analyse and create. Developing not only technical skills, but confidence, empathy and independent ways of thinking. At Marymount, creativity is deeply personal and highly individual. Small class sizes, specialist facilities and personalised guidance allow students to develop their own creative voice while exploring both traditional and emerging forms of artistic and design practice. Students are encouraged to think ambitiously, take creative risks and discover the limitless potential of making. ”
Jim Robertson – Head of Art & Design
Creativity without limits
Art & Design at Marymount develops creativity, critical thinking and confidence through highly personalised teaching, practical making and conceptual exploration. Students are encouraged to experiment, create and discover their own artistic identity while developing specialist skills and responding to real-world creative challenges.
Marymount’s small class sizes and personalised approach allow each student to pursue individual interests, receive meaningful one-to-one mentoring and work with both traditional and high-tech creative methods.
Two distinct disciplines, one creative vision
Art and Design are taught as two distinctive but complementary disciplines:
Visual art explores how imagery, materials and creative processes can communicate ideas and conceptual meaning. Students learn to understand how they see the world and how others experience it.
Design focuses on problem-solving through creative thinking. Students learn to identify challenges, analyse needs and develop practical, human-centred solutions.
Signature differentiators
Students can pursue bespoke interest
Access to high-level facilities
Creative confidence grows through personalised teacher relationships

Humanities
Understanding the world, shaping the future
Humanities at Marymount helps students understand people, societies and global challenges through inquiry, discussion and real-world exploration. Through history, economics, psychology, politics and environmental systems, students develop the knowledge and critical thinking skills needed to engage thoughtfully with an interconnected world.
Why humanities matters
Humanities is about far more than learning facts. It helps students understand how societies function, why change happens and how individuals can influence the world around them.
At Marymount International School London, students learn to analyse complex issues, evaluate perspectives and make connections between historical events and contemporary challenges. Through this process, they become informed, thoughtful and globally minded citizens.
The Marymount approach to Humanities
Humanities learning is globally minded and concept-based, encouraging students to explore diverse cultures, international perspectives and key ideas such as power, identity, conflict, migration and inequality.
Students develop curiosity through inquiry, investigation and real-world issues, while connections with subjects such as English, Religious Studies and the Arts create richer and more meaningful learning experiences.

pageCache.pageTitle: Languages at Marymount London | Our IB Multilingual School
pageCache.text:
Languages
Where languages bring the world closer
A multilingual programme designed around language, literature and acquisition.
Languages at Marymount
Marymount is a genuinely multilingual school, with language learning embedded throughout the Senior School and Sixth Form. Students follow either Language & Literature or Language Acquisition pathways, allowing them to study at a level that reflects their linguistic background, experience and proficiency. English is the language of instruction, and all students continue to develop their English throughout their time at Marymount International School London.
Students can learn a new language, strengthen their English, maintain and develop their mother tongue, and study literature academically in more than one language. Language learning at Marymount is closely connected to identity, culture, communication, confidence and international-mindedness, with many students progressing towards the IB Bilingual Diploma.
Subjects offered:
Marymount offers two distinct language pathways designed to meet students at the right level of linguistic experience and proficiency. Language & Literature is for students studying a language at a high level of fluency, often as a first or mother tongue, with a focus on analysing texts, producing writing and using language effectively. Language Acquisition is designed for students developing an additional language, with learning centred around the four key communication skills of listening, reading, speaking and writing.
Across Marymount’s language provision, students can study English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin and Spanish, with opportunities varying according to year group, proficiency and pathway. In the MYP, students can also receive support to maintain and develop their mother tongue, while the IB Diploma continues the distinction between Studies in Language & Literature and Language Acquisition.

pageCache.pageTitle: IB Personal Project: AI and the Future of Dance | Marymount
pageCache.text:
Personal Project Spotlight: AI & The Future of Dance
For her Personal Project, Marymount student Candy, was interested in how technology and AI might change the future of dance. In her aim to reflect on what makes human performance unique, she created a video that explains her research into AI, robotics, and dance.
Why did you choose this topic?
I started dancing when I was 3, and I have trained in many different styles since, so dance has always been a huge part of my life. What I love most about dancing is being able to express myself freely through movement and connect emotionally with others during performances. Because dance has always been so important to me, I immediately knew I wanted my project to relate to it in some way. I have also always been curious and wanted to learn more about science, technology, robotics, and specifically AI. Overall, I thought that it would be very interesting to learn how the two worlds may collide in the future.
Did you have to do a lot of research?
I did many different types of research, from online browsing to finding books on what AI can currently do and the basics of dance (e.g. from a psychological perspective). I thought it would be important to consider ideas from multiple perspectives, and so I interviewed three different groups of people: dance teachers, dancers, and non-dancers. I collected primary research by asking them questions that I intentionally designed for each group. Based on their responses, I compared how people with different experiences and roles viewed the use of AI and robotics in the dance industry. This was helpful as it helped me gain a wide range of perspectives and, therefore, reach a more balanced conclusion on how AI can potentially impact the dance industry in the future.
Did your opinion about AI and dance change during the process, and did you learn anything new?
Yes definitely! Before, I believed that AI could be intimidating to the dance industry. Now, I realised that, although AI can generate choreography and imitate movement patterns, it still cannot replicate the emotional expression, authenticity and human connection that human dance performances encompass.
I also discovered through the interviews I conducted that many people do not see AI as a replacement for dancers, and especially don’t believe it’s capable of “taking over the dance industry”, but rather can be used as a tool to support the industry
How did you decide what makes human performance unique?
I decided what makes human performance unique by analysing real-life examples or clips of robots dancing versus real-life examples of humans dancing. Using my creative thinking, I created a set of criteria including different aspects that I would compare across. These included formations, timing, and creativity, emotional expression and storytelling, flow and transitions, and audience connection. This allowed me to use my critical thinking to break down the concept into its constituent parts, and through this, I learnt that humans have a greater variety of movements which all flow together and are more natural. I think this was my favourite part of the whole process and really transformed my learning
Thank you, Candy, for sharing your curiosity with us!

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Studies at Marymount London | IB World School
pageCache.text:
Religious Studies
Explore belief. Question deeply. Think for yourself.
Rooted in Marymount’s Catholic identity and enriched by our international community, Religious Studies invites students to explore faith, philosophy and ethics, encounter different perspectives, and develop the knowledge, discernment and critical thinking to engage thoughtfully with the world around them.
Why Religious Studies matters?
Religious Studies at Marymount encourages students to explore some of life’s most important questions: what we believe, how we understand others, and how our values shape the choices we make.
Through the study of faith, culture, ethics and philosophy, students develop the knowledge and confidence to engage thoughtfully with different perspectives. They learn to appreciate the beliefs, traditions and heritage of others while also reflecting more deeply on their own ideas and values.
At the heart of the subject is the development of the whole person. Students are encouraged to become morally aware, globally minded and capable of discernment — thinking critically about complex questions rather than simply accepting easy answers.
Religious Studies is also a rigorous academic discipline. Through discussion, analysis and evaluation, students learn to question, reason and think independently, developing skills that extend far beyond the classroom.
The Marymount approach to Religious Studies
Discussion is central to Religious Studies at Marymount. The classroom is a safe and inclusive environment where students can ask questions, share perspectives and explore complex issues of faith, ethics and philosophy. Every student’s voice is valued, and different beliefs and experiences are welcomed as part of the learning.
Rather than focusing only on difference, students are encouraged to recognise connections between faiths, cultures and experiences. This creates space for thoughtful dialogue, helping them to understand others more deeply while developing and articulating their own ideas.

A classroom built around dialogue
Religious Studies lessons are varied, active and discussion-led. Students learn through dialogue, independent research, group work, peer teaching and creative activities, developing the confidence to question, interpret and evaluate different ideas.
The focus is not simply on what people believe, but on learning to listen, think critically and articulate ideas with clarity and respect.
